diagnosis_of_contaminated_outlier.finding: The D-screen prediction only partly held. kyiv(28,29), the most severe case (D=0.14, T2=12.7us), showed a residual of +1.12 -- consistent with large unmodeled decoherence. But cairo(19,22) (D=0.31) and kyiv(119,120) (D=1.12), also decoherence-affected, showed small NEGATIVE residuals instead of the predicted large positive ones.
diagnosis_of_contaminated_outlier.cause: residual_ratio divides by raw calibrated error p. kyiv(28,29)'s p=0.6013% is roughly 5x smaller than cairo(19,22)'s p=3.132%. The same absolute amount of unmodeled decoherence-driven decay, divided by a much smaller denominator, produces a residual an order of magnitude larger -- not because the physics differs by that much, but because the ratio metric is numerically unstable exactly where p is small. This is the same small-denominator fragility that motivated the D-screen in Entry 021, now shown to affect the residual analysis too, independent of whether decoherence contamination is present.
diagnosis_of_contaminated_outlier.implication: Ratio-based metrics (measured/nominal) should not be trusted at low raw error regardless of D. Absolute residuals (measured minus predicted, not divided by p) would be the numerically stable quantity for any future refit.

verdict: No clean power-law residual survives on the 7 D-screened usable edges: values range -0.008 to +0.184 with inconsistent sign, mean +0.060, and only 7 points across a 0.35%-4.32% error span. This is most consistent with noise, not a real hardware-physics trend -- meaning Entries 017-021's fitted power law was mostly re-deriving the Entry 025 geometric baseline, not discovering new chip physics on top of it. Recommendation for v4: retire the empirically fit variable_forgiveness_ratio() power law in favor of the closed-form baseline directly; let the already-implemented T2-based decoherence term (Entries 023-024) carry the real physical signal instead of asking a ratio fit to do it implicitly and unstably.
